result.reason: H1 is a generic semantic checkpoint for cross-session resumption. The evidence supports value only when the checkpoint holds something a participant selected or some unresolved identity not reconstructable from current owner truth — i.e., the durable-owner/private-commitment concern from T2 (which is TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) — but H1's core (compact summary of reconstructable history) duplicates owner truth. The strongest precedent is T3 (NO_CAPITAL): simpler current-source retrieval suffered no failure, no independent consumer required the extra artifact. Here much of the checkpoint is reconstructable, and only a bounded subset might be truly indispensable. That is exactly the local/partial/optional scope of SCOPED_CAPITAL, not a demonstrated broad repeated-owner transfer like T4/T7/T8. There is no evidence of independent later consumers with stable shared responsibility for the checkpoint, so TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL cannot be supported; but unlike T3, the small non-reconstructable subset gives a bounded useful scope, so NO_CAPITAL is too strong. Hence SCOPED_CAPITAL.

H1 persists a compact semantic checkpoint so future Agents can resume without rereading full history. This closely matches T4 (observation-minimum): a read-only owner exporter plus rebuildable projection that reconstructs trajectories while owner recovery stays independent of the projection. That pattern became TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because multiple owners and formal evaluation reused the same relation semantics. However, H1 differs critically: 'many checkpoint fields are also reconstructable from current owner truth' while a 'smaller subset may contain... commitments or unresolved identities unavailable anywhere else.' This unresolved-identity/commitment aspect echoes T2 (task-continuity), which is the same durable-owner-state capability that survived and transferred. The reconstructable portion alone would be near-NO_CAPITAL duplication (like T6 duplicating truth), but the minority subset that is genuinely not reconstructable elsewhere gives the checkpoint a residual, bounded value: it can preserve private commitments/unresolved external request identity that transcript/session baselines lose. The evidence does not show repeated independent consumption by multiple heterogeneous owners at a stable scope — only a generic Agent-resume convenience over owner truth, with the valuable part being a small subset of not-elsewhere-available fields. That is a bounded/local/partial option-value scope, not demonstrated broad transferable capital. So the prediction is SCOPED_CAPITAL: useful at a bounded residual scope but not yet demonstrated as stable transferred capital.

H2 retains a bounded, digest-bound, scoped alternative pathway beside an ambient mechanism that already completes all currently tested useful work. This mirrors T1 (prototype expresses desired semantics but mature mechanisms already own the mechanics) and T5 (one owner benefits from digest-binding while a second independent owner has not demonstrated shared value), both SCOPED_CAPITAL. The scoped paths are materially faster only on some services, giving option-value/local benefit rather than demonstrated broad reusable value, and they add dedicated services/qualification cost. There is no independent/unowned consumer requiring the scoped paths, unlike T2/T4/T7 which gained transferred value from separate repeated responsibility or independent consumption. Thus the evidence supports a bounded/optional-scope use, not stable transferred capital.

H2 mirrors the T5 configuration-identity pattern: a digest-bound, opaque binding that compares without copying domain semantics, and the change works now (faster on some services) but a second real independent consumer has not demonstrated a shared, stable broader scope — T5 resolved to SCOPED_CAPITAL for exactly that reason. H2 is additionally hedged as option value under future ambient failure, which matches the bounded/local/partial/option-value definition of SCOPED_CAPITAL rather than TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL: ambient networking already completes all currently tested useful work, so there is no demonstrated later independent consumption or repeated responsibility at an evidenced scope, only a speculative option. The visible adaptive value is real but bounded to a local projection and promise of future usefulness, not reused unowned responsibility.

The holdout change is a prior/feedback about responsibility ownership learned from earlier Game work and applied to later rescue behavior. The key differentiators across the evidence are: (a) whether the change's value survives replacement and is consumed by an independent task (T2, T4, T7, T8 = TRANSFERRED), (b) whether it stays owner-internal but requires no broad shared authority yet (T1, T5 = SCOPED), or (c) whether it duplicates existing mature authority or has no independent consumer (T3, T6 = NO_CAPITAL). H3 is a model-visible cognitive/behavioral prior: it changes how the model reasons about custody and responsibility, which parallels T1 (a shared reference/kernel that can express desired semantics but has no demonstrated stable unowned responsibility) and T7 (an agent-led method consumed by later self-audit). Unlike T7, H3's effect on the later multi-turn objective is explicitly indirect and depends on many subsequent policy choices; the evidence states the prior changes reasoning but does not demonstrate later independent consumption of a stable responsibility boundary. It is also not a writable shared authority that duplicates existing truth (so not NO_CAPITAL like T3/T6). The prior has demonstrated value in reshaping reasoning (bounded/option-value), but its transfer to a later independent multi-turn objective is not yet evidenced as a stable reusable responsibility. This most closely matches SCOPED_CAPITAL: useful at a bounded/local/partial scope, not demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

H3 retains a model-visible responsibility/feedback prior and applies it indirectly to later rescue behavior, with effect on later multi-turn objective depending on many subsequent policy choices. This mirrors the T5 pattern (SCOPED_CAPITAL): a shared/transferable-sounding prior or binding that is preserved opaque and useful at a bounded scope, but whose effect depends on downstream composition and lacks a demonstrated independent consumer or repeated stable responsibility. The indirect, policy-dependent pathway means the prior does not itself demonstrate broad transferable reuse; it shapes reasoning about custody locally rather than being a stable, independently-consumed semantic boundary. Explicit evidence says the effect is indirect and conditional, which is insufficient for TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL (which in T2/T4/T7 required later independent consumption or repeated stable responsibility) and not a failed/unpromoted general change (NO_CAPITAL), so SCOPED_CAPITAL is the best-supported prediction.

H4 moves exact, repeated source-history aggregation out of model reasoning into a deterministic Security-local reducer/projection that the model then consumes. This matches the strongest evidenced success pattern in the training data. T4 (TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) is the closest analogue: run-once read-only owner exporters plus a rebuildable selection/query projection reconstruct exact trajectories while owner recovery stays independent of the projection, and multiple owners plus formal evaluation consumed the same relation semantics. H4 likewise keeps the mechanic owner-local (Security), stays read-only/deterministic, and leaves interpretation in the model, so it avoids the failure modes that doomed T6 (global writable authority duplicating truth) and T3 (graph authority with no independent consumer). Unlike T5 (SCOPED_CAPITAL), which stalled because only one non-Evaluation consumer demonstrated a shared schema, H4's projection is a deterministic reducer consumed directly by the model in an existing evaluation loop, analogous to T7's bounded method being consumed by the experiment loop and later by self-audit. The reducer externalizes a precision-sensitive arithmetic burden into a stable, rebuildable projection with an exact escape hatch, which is the reusable-capital signature evidenced by T4 and T7 rather than the SCOPED signature of a single-owner schema experiment (T5) or an unpromoted prototype (T1).

H4 resembles T4 (run-once read-only owner exporters plus a rebuildable projection consumed across owners) but is narrower: T4 made the projection itself the reusable cross-owner capital because multiple independent owners and formal evaluation consumed the same relation semantics without owner recovery depending on the projection. H4 instead moves aggregation into a deterministic Security-local reducer/projection that is consumed only by the model (the owning loop), with a single clear owner (Security) and an explicit escape hatch. The visible evidence does not show a second independent owner or formal evaluator consuming the same projected relation, mirroring T5 (single-owner opaque binding is SCOPED because a second non-Evaluation owner never demonstrated a shared schema). The precision-sensitive correctness burden still rests on the model interpreting the projection, so the reusable value is bounded to the Security-local source-history aggregation scope rather than a demonstrated broad/stably-consumed semantic boundary. I predict SCOPED_CAPITAL: useful as a local owner-scoped projection with escape hatch, not yet demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

H5 (render-review-prior) states a concrete production rule: inspect exact rendered pixels when layout matters, with a direct observable artifact, a bounded correction path, and exact unchanged controls. This closely parallels T8's infrastructure-promotion-rule, which is a reusable rule with a bounded correction path and is TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL, but H5 differs in a key way: its scope is explicitly bounded to ordinary Web/Studio production (expression/layout cases) rather than a stable cross-owner responsibility. The evidence does not demonstrate independent later consumption beyond the original page, nor repeated unowned responsibility; it only demonstrates rule-form + production-relevant bounded scope. This matches the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern (useful at a bounded/local/partial scope), like T1 and T5 which are production-relevant but never demonstrated broad transferable or independently consumed value. Unlike T2/T4/T7 which show later independent consumption across owners, H5 shows only a bounded correction path and intended future use, not observed later reuse. Therefore the evidence supports SCOPED_CAPITAL, not TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL, and clearly not NO_CAPITAL since it is a retained, useful procedure with a bounded correction path.

H5 (render-review-prior) is a retained production rule that prescribes observing exact rendered pixels when expression/layout matters, rather than treating source/build/browser mechanics as proof. This matches the strongest positive evidence pattern in the training set: the durable rules and read-only procedures that earned TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL (T2 durable owner-state lifecycle, T4 read-only exporters with a rebuildable projection consumed by multiple owners and formal evaluation, T7 bounded agent-led method with a direct observable artifact and bounded correction path consumed by experiment loop and later self-audit, T8 reusable rule intended to guide heterogeneous later decisions). H5 has the same structural markers as T8 in particular: it is framed as a retained rule intended for later ordinary production use across multiple Web/Studio pages, not a one-off page fix. Its observable artifact (exact rendered pixels), bounded correction path, and exact unchanged controls mirror the 'direct observable artifact + bounded correction path' feature that repeatedly co-occurs with transferred value (T4, T7), and no evidence suggests an overly broad writable/authority duplication surface (which characterized NO_CAPITAL T3/T6). The rule is small, owner-local, read-only in effect, and does not create a new shared semantic authority, avoiding the failure mode of T1/T3/T6. Since it is designed for repeated independent consumption across later ordinary production work, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is the best-supported prediction.

H6 is a narrow, read-only projection exposing an accessible/currentness view of route affordances, motivated by the concrete repeated need that Agents keep reconstructing routes from raw configuration. This maps most closely to T4/T6 logic: owner-native truth is retained and only a projected view is added, not a new authoritative/writable registry; leaving route selection and effects to the Agent and keeping native evidence reachable avoids a new shared authority or compatibility surface (the failure mode flagged in T1/T3/T6). Because it directly relieves a repeatedly observed reconstruction cost and is consumed read-only across a bounded scope, it earns SCOPED_CAPITAL. It is not TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because the evidence shows only a single, local, option-value scope (Workstation surface), and only one consuming pattern (reconstructing route affordances) rather than later independent/repeated unowned responsibility at a stable broad scope; T7/T8 achieve transfer only when a method/rule is consumed by multiple distinct owners and responsibilities, which is not yet demonstrated here. It is not NO_CAPITAL because the change is motivated by a real repeated failure-to-reuse cost and is deliberately bounded as a non-authoritative projection, matching the promoted pattern in T4/T6.

H6 is a read-only projection that reconstructs route affordances from raw configuration to reduce repeated reconstruction cost, while leaving route selection/effects to the Agent and keeping native evidence reachable, without a central capability registry. This closely matches the successful read-only projection pattern seen in T4/T6 (project owner-native truth read-only, no duplicate writable authority) and avoids the failure mode of T6 (global writable duplicate) and T3 (over-promoting storage/authority before an independent consumer needed it). However, the evidence shows only a bounded, local workflow repeatedly reconstructing route affordances, with no demonstrated independent unowned consumer or repeated cross-owner responsibility for the surface. Unlike T8's promotion rule (which was consumed repeatedly by heterogeneous later decisions as a stable boundary), H6 has not shown independent consumption beyond the internal Computing workflow, so the reuse is scoped and option-value rather than proven broad transferable capital. Given T5 showed a second real non-Evaluation owner was still missing for an analogous opaque binding, H6 similarly remains SCOPED until a second independent consumer or repeated unowned responsibility is evidenced.

H7 carries T8 (the Infrastructure Promotion Rule) forward as a fixed prompt prior into a later heterogeneous set of architecture/owner decisions. T8 itself is TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL because it is a reusable rule intended to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions and is repeatedly consumed. However, H7 does not add a new reusable mechanism or evidence; it merely embeds the rule as a prior. The evidence says it 'adds no new owner facts and may bias different model families differently,' so its transfer as a distinct durable artifact is not evidenced: it is an option-value/guide whose value is bounded and local to steering future decisions rather than a demonstrated repeated independent responsibility. It inherits partial, scoped value rather than stable broad transfer, matching SCOPED_CAPITAL (useful only at a bounded/partial/option-value scope).

H7 carries the Infrastructure Promotion Rule (T8) itself as a fixed prompt prior for later heterogeneous architecture/owner decisions. The evidence for T8's own promotion is strong: it was consumed across heterogeneous decisions (TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL). But H7 is a distinct change — it treats the rule as a static, opaque prompt prior rather than a live rule, and it explicitly adds no new owner facts while risking differential bias across model families. The training evidence shows that a change earns TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL only when later independent consumption or repeated responsibility demonstrates reusable value at stable scope (T2, T4, T7, T8), while mechanisms that are useful only as options/partial views or whose shared schema/boundary is not independently demonstrated remain SCOPED (T1, T5), and changes that only duplicate truth or lack any independent consumer are NO_CAPITAL (T3, T6). H7 is a bounded, option-value carry of prior knowledge: it is plausibly useful as a bias-reducing prior within Computing research, but there is no visible evidence of a distinct independent consumer of the static-prior mechanism itself, no demonstrated generalization across differing model families (which would be required to survive differential bias), and no repeated responsibility yet. It does not add owner facts (so no duplicate-truth NO_CAPITAL), but it also has not demonstrated the transfer to a new stable consumer that separates TRANSFERRED from SCOPED. Therefore SCOPED_CAPITAL is the best-supported prediction: useful only at a bounded/local/partial/option-value scope, not yet demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

H8 is a procedural rule/checklist (analogous to T8's infrastructure-promotion-rule and T7's bounded agent-first method) that externalizes a generic calibration discipline: ask about current consumer, incremental outcome, simpler baseline, recurring cost/coupling, authority fit, and reopen/deletion before choosing a disposition. The training evidence shows that reusable rules and methods which generalize across heterogeneous later decisions and are consumed by multiple independent responsibilities become transferred capital: T7 (agent-first research method, consumed by experiment loop AND self-audit) = TRANSFERRED, and T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule, intended to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions) = TRANSFERRED. In contrast, the failed/unpromoted items (T3, T6) were material mechanisms (graph storage, global usage database) that duplicated a simpler baseline or a truth authority, and the merely-scoped items (T1, T5) were specific shared implementations/schemas whose generality was not yet demonstrated. H8 is not a shared semantic kernel or a writable ownership store; it is a rule-of-thumb that substitutes a static prior with an explicit, repeated calibration procedure, which directly mirrors the generalized reusable-rule pattern evidenced as transferred. It is explicitly applied to a materially different decision family (professional-equipment), demonstrating the cross-domain reproducibility that distinguishes transferred from scoped capital, and it is read-only (no new writable authority or shared schema that could duplicate truth).

H8 is a generalization of the already-evidenced adaptive regularities. T7 (agent-first-research-method, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) established that a bounded reusable method with falsifier, rollback and disposition control is consumed by later independent loops and by self-audit; T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) established that a reusable rule guiding heterogeneous later decisions reaches stable transferred scope. H8 packages exactly the questions those successful transfers repeatedly answered (current consumer, incremental outcome, simpler baseline, recurring cost/coupling, authority fit, reopen/deletion) into a generic calibration procedure, replacing a static prior. The evidence pattern that predicts TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is not implementation size, depth, or persistence, but later independent consumption of a stable reusable method/rule across materially different decision families. H8 is explicitly applied to a materially different professional-equipment decision family, mirroring the cross-domain independent reuse that distinguished the transferred outcomes from SCOPED (T5: single-secondary-composition shown but no shared schema) and NO_CAPITAL (T3/T6: no materially independent consumer). H8 does not overclaim new authority or compatibility surface (unlike T1/T6, which fell to SCOPED/NO for that reason), and it defers ownership/promotion the way T7/T8 do. Therefore the supported prediction is TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL.
